compiled_state.title: [reconciler/architecture]: bidirectional local-wins contract drops legitimate inbound label-ADD when outbound emits spurious REMOVE for same label
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview
Post-#461 (all sync fixes merged + ghost label fix applied), labels probe T3 IB-ADD still fails. The local-wins contract in inbound_differ.py:357-365 correctly suppresses the inbound mutation, but the suppression is over-broad — it also drops legitimate inbound ADDs when outbound emits a spurious REMOVE.

## Scenario
- Local state: [labelprobe]
- Jira state (after Jira-side ADD): [dso-id, labelprobe, ib-added]
- Outbound differ: sees 'local lacks ib-added' → emits REMOVE ib-added (WRONG — local never had it, Jira just got it)
- Inbound differ: sees 'jira has ib-added, local doesn't' → emits ADD ib-added (CORRECT)
- 3bf8 bidir suppression: outbound REMOVE + inbound ADD same label → suppress inbound ADD per local-wins
- Result: ib-added is lost both ways (local doesn't get it; outbound would remove it from Jira if executed)

## Root cause
The outbound differ cannot distinguish 'local removed X' from 'local never had X'. It treats any local-vs-jira diff as a local-side action. When combined with bidir suppression, legitimate inbound-only changes are cancelled.

## Severity
MEDIUM — affects any Jira-side ADD on a bound ticket. Workaround: user can force-add the label locally then re-sync.

## Proposed fix approaches (architectural)
1. **Track 'local intent' explicitly**: outbound differ only emits REMOVE when there's a local TAG_REMOVE event since the binding, not when the local snapshot just lacks the label.
2. **Two-phase sync**: first inbound (jira → local), then outbound (local → jira) against post-inbound snapshot. Eliminates the diff-conflict by serialization.
3. **Snapshot-based binding-time tracking**: at bind time, record local tag baseline; outbound only emits REMOVE for tags present at bind time that local subsequently removed.

## Reproduction
On main (post-#461 merge equivalent: HEAD ~ ee68813cd8) + DSO_RECONCILER_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET=20 bash /tmp/labels-probe.sh — T3 IB-ADD FAIL deterministically.

**code_version**: 1f0032df245a260e8b8d445128d04a739af9e49d

comments.body:
## Approach re-analysis (2026-05-29)

**Option 2 (two-phase sync: inbound-first then refresh+outbound) is REJECTED — breaks local label removal.**

Scenario: local=[A, X], jira=[A, X, dso-id]. User removes X locally → local=[A].
- Inbound runs first against pre-pass snapshot: emits ADD X, applies → local=[A, X]
- Refresh: local=[A, X], jira=[A, X] → outbound emits nothing
- Net: X silently restored locally; user's removal undone.

The PR #457 local-wins suppression is load-bearing precisely because neither differ has a baseline. Reordering does not add information — it inverts which side wins by default.

**Only options 1 and 3 are correct fixes** (both add a baseline so differs can distinguish "local never had X" from "local had X and removed it"):

- **Option 1 — local-intent tracking**: outbound only emits REMOVE when there's a corresponding local TAG_REMOVE event. Requires consuming the event log in outbound_differ (larger surface).
- **Option 3 — binding-time baseline (RECOMMENDED)**: snapshot local tags at bind time, store on binding record. Outbound differ computes diff against (current_local - baseline) intent, suppressing spurious REMOVEs for labels local never had. Smaller schema delta than option 1; preserves local-wins semantics; no orchestration reorder needed.

Updated recommendation: **option 3**. Awaiting user approval before implementation.
